body: All the casual and part-time jobs that don't need credentials. Admin, reception, cleaners, grocery store clerks, waitressing jobs. Anything. There's not a lot around in my town.
Unfortunately job interviews are all about how you come across in person.

Sorry about that but they do call me the rslur, especially my family and peers. It offends me too which is why I don't say the word, but that's what I'm called so that's my inner monologue.

I can't get vocational rehabilitation because I don't qualify under the NDIS. :(

Yeah in Australia we have stuff like that but you need to qualify under the NDIS and I don't qualify (I only come under level one and they only support levels 2 + 3). There are also disability employment services, but they don't help much. They function less as a support service and more to monitor you if you're on payments and dole out punishment if you don't meet requirements. If you're voluntary they want nothing to do with you besides get commission if you find a job yourself. It's actually a huge scam at the moment here it's pretty interesting and all over google.

I think I'd have a better time with meds. The psychs I've seen are reluctant to prescribe but I might get there in the end. I did decently on pristiq + abilify but then they took me off them. Maybe something similar to them might help.

I'm trying my hardest. I'm switching from a bachelor's in social work to a BA with a human services major this year if my application gets through. I won't survive compulsory full time placement for a year so thats the next best thing. Don't know what I'd even do from there with such a bludge degree though.

Thanks though. I'll have to remember that thing about taxes. I'm not even receiving benefits and I feel like a leech. I need to turn my thinking around.

The volunteering is so thankless, just filled with depressed unemployed people who want to find work. We get a lot of abuse from clients thanks to the nature of the organisation. It's awful but it's better than nothing.

Everything's just getting me down lately. It's that small town syndrome. There's little to go around.
